meta.mechanism: PCSK9 inhibitor (fully human monoclonal antibody); blocks PCSK9-mediated LDL receptor degradation so more hepatic LDL receptors recycle and clear LDL; lowers LDL-C ~55-60% on top of statin
meta.indication: prevention of a first major adverse cardiovascular event in high-risk patients without prior myocardial infarction or stroke (qualifying coronary, cerebrovascular or peripheral atherosclerosis, or high-risk diabetes) with LDL-C >=90 mg/dL (or non-HDL-C >=120 or apoB >=80 mg/dL) on optimized lipid-lowering therapy

n_randomized.quote: A total of 12,257 patients were randomly assigned to receive evolocumab (6129 patients) or placebo (6128) and were included in the efficacy analyses.
n_randomized.note: Registry S3: 12,301 enrolled; 'data from 44 participants were excluded from all results analyses' because of 'site-wide serious breaches and good clinical practice (GCP) violations'. Design paper S5 abstract also gives 12,301.

median_followup.note: Registry S3 time frame: 'median (min, max) time on trial was 55.2 (0.0, 72.7) months'. Topline press release S2 said 'a median of approximately 4.5 years'.

primary_endpoint.value: Dual primary end points: (1) 3-point MACE = CHD death, MI or ischemic stroke; (2) 4-point MACE = 3-point MACE or ischemia-driven arterial revascularization
primary_endpoint.quote: The two primary end points were a composite of death from coronary heart disease, myocardial infarction, or ischemic stroke (3-point MACE) and a composite of 3-point MACE or ischemia-driven arterial revascularization (4-point MACE).
primary_endpoint.note: Sample size was based on the triple (3-point) endpoint (S4). The outcome block below uses 3-point MACE; 4-point MACE: 747 vs 907, HR 0.81 (0.73-0.89), P<0.001.

inclusion_key_criteria.value: Men >=50 / women >=55 to <80 years; no prior MI or stroke; LDL-C >=90 mg/dL or non-HDL-C >=120 mg/dL or apoB >=80 mg/dL on optimized lipid-lowering therapy; significant CAD, cerebrovascular atherosclerosis, PAD, or high-risk diabetes, plus at least one high-risk criterion; TG <500 mg/dL
inclusion_key_criteria.quote: Lipid Criteria: Low-density lipoprotein cholesterol (LDL-C) ≥ 90 mg/dL (≥ 2.3 mmol/L) or non high-density lipoprotein cholesterol (non-HDL)-C ≥ 120 mg/dL (≥ 3.1 mmol/L), or apolipoprotein B ≥ 80 mg/dL (≥ 1.56 µmol/L).
inclusion_key_criteria.note: Registry age criterion: 'Adult participants ≥ 50 (men) or ≥ 55 (women) to ˂ 80 years of age'. Exclusions include 'MI or stroke prior to randomization' and 'Triglycerides ≥ 500 mg/dL'. ACC summary S7: 45% CAD, 10% cerebrovascular disease, 17% PAD, 60% diabetes (49% high-risk diabetes).

planned_events.unit: patients with a primary triple (3-point MACE) endpoint
planned_events.quote: a total sample size of at least 12000 subjects, with approximately 751 subjects experiencing a primary triple component endpoint, is required to ensure approximately 90.5% power (Shih, 1995) based on a 2-sided log-rank test
planned_events.note: Also about 1254 quadruple (4-point) endpoint events (95.6% power). Design paper S5 abstract (public 2023-12-29): 'at least 751 patients experience an adjudicated triple endpoint, at least 1254 experience an adjudicated quadruple endpoint, and the median follow-up is ≥4.5 years.' Observed: 779 triple, 1654 quadruple.

assumed_rrr.quote: 0.77 for primary triple component endpoint and 0.80 for primary quadruple component endpoint.
assumed_rrr.note: Preceding text (p. 19): 'the anticipated HRs over the duration of this entire study for the primary endpoints will be' (sentence continues across the page break). Derived from an anticipated LDL-C difference: 'it is anticipated that the LDL-C difference between the evolocumab and placebo arms will be approximately 1.7 mmol/L at the midpoint of the trial' with a 12-month treatment lag. Assumed placebo annual event rates 1.63% (triple) and 2.72% (quadruple). RRR 0.23 = 1 - 0.77 (derived).

power.quote: is required to ensure approximately 90.5% power (Shih, 1995) based on a 2-sided log-rank test
power.note: 95.6% power for the quadruple endpoint at ~1254 events.

alpha.unit: two-sided, per primary endpoint (overall 0.05 with truncated Hochberg)
alpha.quote: The two-sided 0.025 significance level of type I error is used for each of the primary estimands.
alpha.note: Multiplicity (SAP section 7): 'The truncated Hochberg procedure is based on the 2-sided alpha level of 0.05'; the larger primary p-value is tested at 0.0375, and if it succeeds both primaries succeed. One interim analysis at 75% of events with Haybittle-Peto two-sided alpha 0.001.

stopped_early.note: Not stopped early. Registry S3 overall status COMPLETED, primary completion 2025-07-25 (actual), recruitment 'between June 2019 and July 2025'. The SAP S4 interim analysis (75% of events) required 'A two-sided p < 0.001 in both primary pre-specified endpoints with consistency in major subgroups and a definite reduction in coronary, cardiovascular, and total mortality' to stop; the trial ran to its planned median follow-up (4.6 years).

baseline.quote: The median baseline LDL-C was 122 mg/dL (IQR, 104-149 mg/dL) on local lab testing.
baseline.note: = 3.16 mmol/L (derived). Lipid substudy (n=2014, central lab) median baseline 115 mg/dL (S7, S8). Galli S9: 'Baseline LDL and ApoB levels were 122 and 102 mg/dL, respectively.'

baseline.quote: Baseline LDL and ApoB levels were 122 and 102 mg/dL, respectively.
baseline.note: Secondary source (editorial citing S1). Whether median or mean is not stated. NEJM full text not read.
Lp(a) measured at baseline in 7557 of 12,257 patients (prespecified analysis).
NOT FOUND: baseline non-HDL-C not reported in any source read (NEJM Table 1 not accessed).

biomarker_effects.method: central-lab lipid substudy in a randomly selected subgroup (assay method not captured)
biomarker_effects.quote: At 48 weeks, the mean percentage change in LDL-C with evolocumab compared with placebo was −55%, corresponding to an absolute difference of −63 mg/dL.
biomarker_effects.location: Section 'Evolocumab in primary prevention: The VESALIUS-CV Study'
biomarker_effects.note: Secondary source (open-access review in PMC, citing S1). Same numbers in ACC summary S7 ('LDL-C reduction: 55%', 'Absolute reduction: 63 mg/dL') and median achieved LDL-C 45 vs 109 mg/dL in S6 (Amgen press release). NEJM full text (with CI) not read. Lp(a) paper S10 abstract: LDL-C reduced by 66.8 mg/dL (Lp(a) >105 nmol/L) and 61.1 mg/dL (Lp(a) <=105 nmol/L) at 48 weeks.

biomarker_effects.quote: At 48 weeks, the mean percentage change in LDL-C with evolocumab compared with placebo was −55%, corresponding to an absolute difference of −63 mg/dL.
biomarker_effects.note: DERIVED conversion: 63 mg/dL / 38.67 = 1.63 mmol/L. The SAP (S4) anticipated an LDL-C difference of ~1.7 mmol/L at the trial midpoint. CTT check (derived, not from source): 0.78^1.63 = 0.67 expected RR for a full ~5-year effect vs observed HR 0.75 for 3-point MACE over median 4.6 y; the SAP's own lag-adjusted expectation was HR 0.77.

biomarker_effects.quote: Evolocumab also significantly reduced other atherogenic lipid parameters compared with placebo, with mean percentage reductions of −47% for non-HDL cholesterol and −44% for apolipoprotein B.
biomarker_effects.location: Section 'Evolocumab in primary prevention: The VESALIUS-CV Study'
biomarker_effects.note: Secondary source (review citing S1). Absolute non-HDL-C change NOT FOUND.

biomarker_effects.quote: Evolocumab also significantly reduced other atherogenic lipid parameters compared with placebo, with mean percentage reductions of −47% for non-HDL cholesterol and −44% for apolipoprotein B.
biomarker_effects.location: Section 'Evolocumab in primary prevention: The VESALIUS-CV Study'
biomarker_effects.note: Secondary source (review citing S1). Absolute apoB change NOT FOUND.

biomarker_effects.quote: After 48 weeks, evolocumab reduced LDL-C (low-density lipoprotein cholesterol) by 66.8 mg/dL and Lp(a) by 38.0 nmol/L in patients with baseline Lp(a) >105 nmol/L versus 61.1 mg/dL and 6.0 nmol/L in those with baseline Lp(a) ≤105 nmol/L.
biomarker_effects.note: Only stratum-specific absolute reductions are given (38.0 nmol/L above 105 nmol/L; 6.0 nmol/L at or below). Whole-trial percentage Lp(a) change NOT FOUND; whether placebo-adjusted not stated in the abstract. Galli S9 cites a class effect of 'lower Lp(a) levels by 19%–27%' (from earlier trials).

biomarker_effects.quote: At the end of the dosing interval at week 12, the mean LDL-C concentrations were reduced generally dose dependently by AMG 145 every 2 weeks (ranging from 41·8% to 66·1%; p<0·0001 for each dose vs placebo) and AMG 145 every 4 weeks (ranging from 41·8% to 50·3%; p<0·0001).
biomarker_effects.note: Phase 2 dose-ranging of evolocumab (AMG 145) on statin background; upper end (140 mg Q2W, the VESALIUS-CV dose) shown. Whether placebo-subtracted is not explicit in the abstract.

biomarker_effects.quote: At 48 weeks, the least-squares mean percentage reduction in LDL cholesterol levels with evolocumab, as compared with placebo, was 59%, from a median baseline value of 92 mg per deciliter (2.4 mmol per liter) to 30 mg per deciliter (0.78 mmol per liter) (P<0.001).
biomarker_effects.note: Different trial (secondary prevention, same drug and dose). -1.45 mmol/L absolute from FOURIER main text (see golden case fourier). Public 2017, before VESALIUS-CV readout.

hr.unit: hazard ratio (primary 3-point MACE: CHD death, MI or ischemic stroke)
hr.quote: A 3-point MACE event occurred in 336 patients (5-year Kaplan–Meier estimate, 6.2%) in the evolocumab group, as compared with 443 (8.0%) in the placebo group (hazard ratio, 0.75; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65 to 0.86; P<0.001).
hr.note: Second primary (4-point MACE): 747 (13.4%) vs 907 (16.2%), HR 0.81 (0.73-0.89), P<0.001. Registry S3 gives identical HRs (Cox model, stratified 2-sided log-rank). Secondary (S3): MI HR 0.64 (0.52-0.79); CV death/MI/ischemic stroke HR 0.73 (0.64-0.84); CHD death HR 0.89 (0.68-1.16), p=0.39 (hierarchy broke here); CV death HR 0.79 (0.64-0.98); all-cause death HR 0.80 (0.70-0.91); ischemic stroke HR 0.79 (0.62-1.01). Absolute 5-year KM difference 1.8 points (derived 8.0-6.2).

p.quote: hazard ratio, 0.75; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.65 to 0.86; P<0.001
p.note: Registry S3: '< 0.001', '2-sided log-rank test stratified by randomization factors'. ACC summary S7 reports p<0.0001.

events_treatment.quote: A 3-point MACE event occurred in 336 patients (5-year Kaplan–Meier estimate, 6.2%) in the evolocumab group
events_treatment.note: Evolocumab arm N=6129. Registry S3 outcome table: 336.

events_control.quote: as compared with 443 (8.0%) in the placebo group
events_control.note: Placebo arm N=6128. Registry S3 outcome table: 443. Total 779 vs 751 planned.

safety_signals.value: No between-group difference in safety events
safety_signals.quote: No evidence of a between-group difference was seen in the incidence of safety events.
safety_signals.note: Safety collection was limited (see next item).

safety_signals.value: Serious adverse events 1726/6125 (28.2%) evolocumab vs 1772/6122 (28.9%) placebo
safety_signals.note: Numbers read from the registry results table (no quotable sentence); percentages derived. Serious diabetes mellitus 8 vs 16, hemorrhagic stroke 2 vs 3, cataract 9 vs 8 (evolocumab vs placebo).

safety_signals.value: Limited safety ascertainment: only serious AEs and AEs leading to discontinuation were collected
safety_signals.quote: Only treatment-emergent adverse events that were serious or led to discontinuation were captured.
safety_signals.note: Review S8: 'Safety analyses were limited to the collection of adverse events leading to treatment discontinuation and serious adverse events.' So new-onset diabetes and injection-site reactions were not systematically captured as in FOURIER.

safety_signals.quote: No new safety signals were observed.

genetics.finding: PCSK9 nonsense (loss-of-function) mutations associated with 28% lower LDL-C and 88% lower CHD risk in black ARIC participants
genetics.quote: 2.6 percent had nonsense mutations in PCSK9; these mutations were associated with a 28 percent reduction in mean LDL cholesterol and an 88 percent reduction in the risk of CHD

genetics.finding: Mendelian randomization: PCSK9 and HMGCR variants give nearly identical CV protection per unit LDL-C lowering
genetics.effect: OR 0.81 (0.74-0.89) per 10 mg/dL lower LDL-C for PCSK9
genetics.quote: Variants in PCSK9 and HMGCR were associated with nearly identical protective effects on the risk of cardiovascular events per decrease of 10 mg per deciliter (0.26 mmol per liter) in the LDL cholesterol level: odds ratio for cardiovascular events, 0.81 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.74 to 0.89) for PCSK9

genetics.finding: LDL-C is causal; CTT: ~22% fewer major vascular events per 1 mmol/L LDL-C reduction, similar in all patient types
genetics.quote: similar proportional reductions in major vascular events per 1·0 mmol/L LDL cholesterol reduction were found in all types of patient studied (rate ratio [RR] 0·78, 95% CI 0·76-0·80; p<0·0001)

genetics.finding: Clinical validation of the same drug: FOURIER (evolocumab, secondary prevention) reduced MACE

consensus_explanation.summary: VESALIUS-CV met both primary end points with a clear margin: 3-point MACE HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.65-0.86) and 4-point MACE HR 0.81 (0.73-0.89), from 779 triple-endpoint events against 751 planned over a median 4.6 years. The effect matched what the mechanism and the design predicted: a genetically validated target (PCSK9 loss of function, PCSK9/HMGCR Mendelian randomization), a placebo-adjusted LDL-C reduction of 55% (63 mg/dL, about 1.6 mmol/L) to a median of 45 mg/dL, and a sponsor-prespecified HR of 0.77 based on an expected 1.7 mmol/L difference. The authors, editorialists and the ACC summary read it as extending the FOURIER result to patients with atherosclerosis or high-risk diabetes but no prior MI or stroke, supporting lower LDL-C targets earlier on the risk continuum; MI fell 36% and a prespecified diabetes-without-atherosclerosis subgroup showed a similar benefit (HR 0.69). Experts' caveats concern interpretation rather than validity: absolute benefit is smaller than in secondary prevention (1.8 points at 5 years for 3-point MACE), two-thirds of patients had documented atherosclerosis so it is not 'true' primary prevention, mortality reductions (all-cause HR 0.80) are exploratory because CHD death broke the hierarchy, safety collection was limited to serious AEs, only ~20% received ezetimibe, and cost-effectiveness is open.

open_questions: NEJM full text and supplement not read (paywall). Lipid effects (LDL-C -55% / -63 mg/dL, non-HDL-C -47%, apoB -44%) were read only in secondary sources (S7, S8) and the CIs are not captured.
Baseline non-HDL-C and the whole-trial Lp(a) % reduction NOT FOUND; Lp(a) effect available only by stratum (S10).

LDL-C mmol/L change (-1.63) is a derived conversion of -63 mg/dL; it comes from the 2014-patient lipid substudy at 48 weeks, not a time-averaged whole-trial difference (annual study-drug discontinuation 4.5%/yr per S8 would dilute the time-averaged difference).
Alpha: each primary was sized at two-sided 0.025 (S4); overall family-wise alpha 0.05 via truncated Hochberg. Calculator input uses 0.025 for the 3-point endpoint.

Mortality: all-cause HR 0.80 (0.70-0.91) and CV death HR 0.79 are nominal/exploratory because CHD death (HR 0.89, p=0.39) broke the hierarchical testing; the prespecified mortality paper (S11) argues for a survival benefit.
Safety data were limited to serious AEs and AEs leading to discontinuation (S6, S8), so lower-grade events (injection-site reactions, new-onset diabetes) are not comparable with FOURIER.
Population label: 67% had documented atherosclerosis; experts (S7) caution this is not 'true' primary prevention. The diabetes-without-atherosclerosis subgroup (S12, HR 0.69) partly addresses this.

TCTMD news coverage (2025-11-08) reported an absolute 1.8% (3-point) and 2.8% (4-point) reduction and a comment by S. Nissen that only ~20% received ezetimibe; read through a summarizing fetch tool only, so not quoted or used as a fact.
